utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we continue with the witness, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Krgovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, good afternoon, Mr. Borbeli. I hope that you're doing fine and I hope that we can continue with this examination of ours. If you don't feel well during the examination, please feel free to tell us, we are going to take a break so that you could pull yourself together. So please, at any point, if you feel you're not feeling well, just tell us?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, yesterday, or rather on Friday, when we stopped, I asked you something about what happened in Samac between the 17th and 18th of April; however, we're going back to an episode that you mentioned during your examination when you saw that group of young men, Muslims, in the hallway of your building, you said that among them you recognised one of your fellow citizens, that that was the waiter from the pizza parlour of the Bicic brothers you said that you could not remember his name. Do you perhaps know what his last name is?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, does he live somewhere near you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lives in the same street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Exhibit P61 ter and P61 -- and P62 ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Borbeli, would you please take a look at these documents. Please look at photographs of this man. Tell me, is that the young man that you saw in your building, in the hallway of your building that night?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: His father's name was Sabrija, this man's father's name was Sabrija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do [Realtime transcript read in error "Do I"].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the young man that you saw in the hallway that night?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, I don't need the document any longer, thank you. Mr. Borbeli, now I'm going to ask you the following: Tell me, in the period after the 17th of April when we talked about the 18th of April, you mentioned that you saw a vehicle on which there was a soldier who was inviting people over a megaphone to hand in their weapons, that's what you said. Now tell me, on that day, in your street, in the street of Pero Bosic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One correction in the transcript, page 2 line 14, the answer says "do I" and actually it was "I do." So maybe this is something that my colleague should clarify this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No that can be corrected because the two words are there on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a tank in that day on the street - I'm sorry because not all of my questions in the transcript because I didn't finish?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, on the 18th of April, did you see Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your street, I mean. I mean in your street?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, tell me, what was the situation like in Bosanski Samac during those first few days with regard to electricity, were there power cuts during those first few days?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no power for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say in relation to the 17th of April how long after the 17th of April there was a power cut, you don't have to give us an exact date, could you just give us an approximation, 10 days, 15 days?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For 17 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what about the telephones, did they stop working in Samac after a while?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, immediately the telephones stopped working too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did the telephones stop working for everyone?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say everyone -- MR. DI FAZIO: Right, if my friend's going to clarify the basis of that question, then I have nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say everyone, does that pertain to all citizens or were there differences along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This pertained to all citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you to wait for the end of my question and then give your answer because there seems to be an overlapping all the time and we shouldn't make the work of the interpreters too difficult so please pause for a few seconds after having heard my question. Mr. Borbeli, when did the telephones start working again in Samac and when did the power supply continue?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well not much time went by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993 or was it 1992, could you pinpoint a year?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I was not in the apartment from the 17th of May onwards so I don't know exactly when the telephones started working again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the telephones of all citizens reconnected?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a special procedure, did one have to submit an application?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever wanted to submitted an application, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in the period 1992/1993 when you returned to your apartment, was it possible to communicate by telephone with Croatia, with a part of Bosnia and Herzegovina that was under the control of the Muslims and the Croats or were there other ways of communication?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember because I did not have a telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, I'm going to finish with this subject and we're going to move on to a period that is different, that is to say, the second half of May, did anybody come to see you in the second half of May, did anybody come to your apartment after the 17th of May?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th of May, a policeman came and he said: Get ready. In five minutes, you are going with me. And I asked him where. And he said: Down by the department store. I got ready in five minutes and I left with him going to the department store. When I got there, I saw a group of citizens, perhaps about 25 or 30 of them who were waiting there and I asked my neighbour, what are you looking for here? And he said we're waiting for a truck to go, I said where, and he said Crkvina. And the truck came shortly. We went to Crkvina. We were put up at the football stadium and we stayed there until the afternoon, perhaps 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. Then we came back --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Borbeli. Could you just pause for a second. I want to put a few questions to you in relation to that. Tell me, who took you to Crkvina, who escorted you to Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who guarded you while you were at the stadium in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was the military in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it those people in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's camouflage uniform as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you spent an afternoon there and where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we were driven to Samac to the secondary school there, to the gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Borbeli, during those first few days, while you were at the secondary school or rather while you were there, how many people were there with you approximately, you don't have to give us an exact number?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was close to 300 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, when you -- did you talk to those people and if you talked to them did they tell you why they were brought there, did they say anything about weapons, if they had weapons?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked some of those people who came with me together from the stadium if they had weapons and they said, well, yes, I did and I handed the weapons over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after they handed the weapons over, were they brought over to the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those people from, the ones who had the weapons, were they from villages or from the town?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were villagers, I think, from Zasavica, Hasic, Gornji and Donji and Hrvatska Tisina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their age, were they of different ages or were they all more or less the same age?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were younger people and there were quite old people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, do you know whether those people were questioned in relation to the weapons, was any investigation conducted?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I was never questioned myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking about you, I'm asking about those people who were there, we'll come back to you later. Those people who had the weapons, were they questioned? MR. DI FAZIO: The witness has said he doesn't know about that. That's the end of the matter, I would have thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, did anybody question you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, how much time did you spend at the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three months, perhaps, three months and seven days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what the conditions were like, what did you sleep on, did you get any food?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conditions were not good. We did receive food, but not enough. We slept on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any possibility for you to receive food from the outside, did citizens bring you food?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning, the citizens brought us food, perhaps for a month or two; however, later, the Red Cross sent food for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, on behalf of the Red Cross, brought the food for you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaso and Sveto [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, could you please tell us if you were visited by a doctor, was there any medical staff?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The doctors came as needed, every other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, another clarification of the transcript, on page 7, line 25, it says Vaso and Sveto and it is actually one person, Sveto Vasovic, Vasovic Sveto.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You answered my question about the doctors, but did any nurses also come to see you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequent were the visits by the doctors and how frequent were the visits by the nurses?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The nurses came almost every morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the doctors?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to need, every second or third day, if anybody needed a doctor, they would get one, a doctor would be requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, could you please tell me if you were beaten in the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they beat the other detainees who were with you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time that I was there, perhaps this happened on a couple of occasions that some younger men were beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the number of the detainees who were in the secondary school, how many of them were actually beaten?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me, except for Sveto Vasovic, did anybody else come from the Red Cross to ask you if you wanted to go on an exchange?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a Red Cross official came and she asked who wanted to -- who did not want to be exchanged and I said that I did not wish to be exchanged, some other people also spoke up so perhaps there were about nine of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this official of the Red Cross write that down?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she had a large notebook with her and this was written down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I mentioned Sveto Vasovic, I did not formulate my question exactly. Who asked you, Sveto Vasovic or this official whether you wanted to be exchanged or not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This woman, this official did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether that was a woman from the local Red Cross or from the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the local Red Cross. I knew her slightly, but I knew her by sight, I didn't actually know her very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, sir, when did you leave the secondary school and when you left, did something happen at the end of August and did you go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I go? Did I leave the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave the secondary school and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A police officer came and asked for 16 people who were to work in Zasavica and I volunteered. He needed 16 people. This happened very quickly, people volunteered and we left that same day for Zasavica for work duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me, during your stay at the secondary school, did you ever see Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend at Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Zasavica sometime in mid-August and I was exchanged at the beginning of September. This was probably then about 17 days that I spent at Zasavica, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me where you lived at Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in a private house at an acquaintance of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what you did at Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We slaughtered pigs and prepared meat for the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions in Zasavica, did you have enough food, did you have enough water, what were the sanitary conditions like?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conditions in Zasavica were good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's something in the transcript that needs to be clarified, could you please tell me how time did you spend in Zasavica? As far as I understood you, you said from mid-August until early September?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 17 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if you remember, were there any police in Zasavica itself, did you see any police officers there? What was the situation there? Did anybody guard you if you saw it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not guarded in Zasavica, we were like free. When we had work, we worked and when we didn't have any work, we were staying in the houses where we lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how you left Zasavica? You said that you were called for the exchange at the beginning of September, so could you please tell me who came to inform you and where you went from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening at about 9.00, a person came who was there with us, a detainee and he said to me: Get ready by 10.00, a truck will come. You're going to be exchanged. I said: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me if you did get ready?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did get ready. I came up to the truck which was standing at the crossroads, then I was taken to Samac to the elementary school. I spent the night there and the next day, I was exchanged. MR. DI FAZIO: It's just not clear to me and I suggest it should be clarified, is the witness saying that someone came at 9.00 at night and to get ready by 10.00 at night, that is, that evening, because it's not entirely clear to me if Mr. Krgovic could just clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes and another clarification, because I was listening very carefully to what the witness was saying and on page 11, line 12, it was translated, "I was exchanged," and this is not actually what the witness was saying and because I was informed by Mr. Krgovic about the testimony of this witness and he actually said, I was taken to the exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's get clarification because at the beginning the witness had said he had refused to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would just like to clarify the first thing stated by my learned friend, the Prosecutor. This man who came, he told you at 9.00 to get ready by 10.00 that evening or by the next day?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That same evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me, you told this woman from the Red Cross that you did not wish to be exchanged; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go by truck from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the elementary school in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one night and then the next morning to the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when did you leave in the morning, could you please tell me who took you out from the elementary school? Who was at the door guarding the elementary school where you spent the night?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you leave the elementary school, did you go directly to the trucks?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a roll call, people were called out and that's how we went to the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who called out the names?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were a lot of people there so I didn't really see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me if you saw Miroslav Tadic in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, how many buses left for the exchange; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, two buses left for the exchange, one from Samac and another one was from somewhere else, perhaps from Derventa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where you were going to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were going to the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it that you stopped first?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came to Bosanska Gradiska, we couldn't get passage there, the UNPROFOR did not let us cross over the bridge, over the Sava River to Croatia, so we waited for about five hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where the buses stopped in Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to leave the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those who wanted to could go out to drink something, to cool down. I didn't leave the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they were able to go out and drink something, what did you mean, did you have water and juices with you in the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was water, there were juices and people were eager to go out and sit in a garden of the restaurant, so several people came out of the bus and sat down outside to have a beer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four to five hours we waited to cross over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left, where did you set out for?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we set out, we crossed the bridge over the Sava River and we were going to the -- to Dragalovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got there, did you leave the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we got there and we left the bus. Miroslav Tadic came up to us and said: Men, those of you who do not want to go to the exchange do not have to and if you want to go back to your homes, you can. And I said right away, that's what I want.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that? Was anybody there that you could talk to who asked you if you wanted to go over to the other side, could you please describe this event a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We crossed over and we lined up two by two and I saw the International Red Cross. They had a large red cross on their chest so that was the International Red Cross and they explained to us there and then how the exchange was going to proceed, who wanted to proceed, yes, who did not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say the International Red Cross, was this some foreigner or was this a local man, the one you described with the red cross on his chest?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a foreigner because I saw when I said no, the other one made a mark and then spoke to him and I saw that he was a foreigner. Then it was clear to me that this was the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, over there where you expressed your positions, was Miroslav Tadic present there or any representatives of the Serb side? Did you see them there at that spot?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Borbeli, apart from you, did anybody else say that they did not want to cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven more people said so. They didn't want to go any further to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can, could you please give us the names of these people?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marosevic, Mato; Alojz Balogh; Stipo Vukovic; Ivan Lonac; a Bosniak, Alija Cosic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, these people who stated their views, namely that they want to cross over to the other side, did they actually go?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They returned together with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to the people who said that they wanted to cross over to the Croatian side, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these people who said that they did not want to cross to the to the other side, what happened to them, what happened to you, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean that particular moment of the exchange, at the exchange, what did you do at that very spot, did you enter the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We immediately entered the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who entered the bus in order to return to Samac together with you or rather did anybody else enter the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic was there, he returned together with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Serbs who had come from the other side, were any of them with you on the bus?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an exchange from Slavonski Brod, that is where Serbs were exchanged as well, and then we went together to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, tell me, were any known people from Samac on the bus together with you, people who then crossed over to the Croatian side, somebody that you knew?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't find this very clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to you, and these people who returned, do you know any of the people who were on the bus with you who had set out for the exchange and who did not return to Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, you mean they went further on, you mean they went further on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I knew quite a few of these people. Dragan Delic, I know. Then Barucic, Franjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit D3/3 ter. [Interpretation] D3/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, please look at this list.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, now -- am I supposed to say who did not go back, who went further on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, look at this list and tell me are the names of the persons you mentioned who did not go for an exchange, people who returned to Samac the ones that you mentioned are they on this list?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are, Vukovic, Stipo; Balogh Alojz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please just give me the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 -- do you want me to give you the serial number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The serial number and the name?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1. Vukovic, Stipo; 2. Balogh Alojz; Kikic Stjepan, number five; Marosevic Mato, number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see Lonac Ivan somewhere there, under number 8?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Juric Mato, 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at number 27, Cosic Alija, is that what you see there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. Lukac Dragan, 25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cosic Alija, 27?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Cosic Alija, 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Borbeli. Mr. Usher, thank you. I don't need the document any further, you can take it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, when you boarded the bus, you set out for Samac, did you stop anywhere on the way?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We returned the same way via Gradiska to Odzak. We got there when it was almost midnight and we had dinner, well, when we had dinner, Miroslav Tadic said: Men, I'm going to pay for dinner, perhaps some people do have money and perhaps others do not. After that, we came to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Borbeli, did you find out later on who came looking for you or whether anybody came looking for you to go for an exchange?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out but when the war was over in 1996 in the month of May when I met up with my sister and nephew in Orasje, it is only then that I found out. Before that, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they the ones who were looking for you, asking for you to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Borbeli, after Odzak, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went home towards Samac and we did come to Samac. It was after midnight, perhaps it was even about 1.30, then we stopped by the Serb church and I asked Miroslav Tadic whether I should report to the authorities the next day and he said: No, do you have any place to go. And I said: Well I have my own apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people who were with you, who returned from the exchange, did they also come out in Samac and go to their homes?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this was close for us, Stipo Vukovic and I got off there by the church because he has a daughter who is married there and I have a relative where I left the key of the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you return to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned the next day. I spent the night there at my relative's place and the next day, I went to the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people who returned with you from the exchange, did they also return to their apartments?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do some of them live in Samac until the present day?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the present day, they've been living in their apartments and houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have any of them died in the mean time?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this Alija Cosic died and Ivan Lonac did too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Ivan Lonac before the war, what position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivan Lonac, what position did he hold before the war?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was commander of the police as of late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is he by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people who returned from the exchange together with you, what are they by ethnicity except for Alija Cosic who you said was a Bosniak, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rest were Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Borbeli, when you returned to your apartment, had it been broken into, had somebody moved into it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the apartment had not been touched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, I'm going to ask you something about living conditions in Samac after your return and I'm just interested in the period until the end of 1993 because that is the period that is included in the indictment. Tell me, in that period, did you live in your apartment in Samac until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Borbeli, did you receive your pension?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, regularly. As soon as I came back from the exchange, the very same month, I received my pension.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to resubmit an application or something?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just gave my relative the receipt for my last pension and before I went for the exchange, I gave it to her and then when I came back, I received my first next pension.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive it regularly throughout the war including this period until 1993?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, regularly, but one could not live on that. Money was worthless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why? Was there an inflation?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was big inflation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did all pensioners receive such pensions?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody, regardless, regardless of ethnic affiliation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, did you receive humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, who did you receive it from and where did you collect it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received it from the Red Cross and there was this big warehouse across the street from the SUP, there was a big warehouse there and that is where humanitarian aid was being handed out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what did you receive by way of humanitarian aid, what was its structure?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, tins, flour, oil, sugar, the bare necessities. Also some toiletries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the living condition in Samac like, was there any shelling after your return from the exchange?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Living conditions were very hard and all of that was because of the shelling. No one ever knew what kind of shelling would take place and when and you always had to be cautious, seek shelter, not walk around town or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did people leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. People did what ever they could do, they left and one noticed from year to year that the town was getting empty. I, as one of those who remained, realised that this was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how these people left Samac? Was there a semi-legal way of getting out?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people left Samac, they made documents, those who went to Serbia so they could go to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what this means, what does it mean to make a document? Does that mean false documents with somebody else's name?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only a personal identity card was needed, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Krgovic I'm just wondering about your question at line 8 at page 21, when you asked, "Was there a semi-legal way of getting out?" I'm just wondering what you mean by semi-legal as such?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a illegal way, these personal identity cards, I wanted to explain what was legal and what was not legal because during the preparation of this witness, he was the one who used this term so I would like to explain or I would like him to explain what he meant by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, could you please -- well, my question refers to members of the Croat and Muslim ethnicity, did they make identity cards with some other people's names and in that way, did they go to Serbia and did they have to pay a certain amount of money for that, is that what you meant when you mentioned this?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those identity cards were made as if a Serb was going; however, it was not a Serb who was going but a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Serbs leaving Samac as well?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody was leaving, whoever wanted to go went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, I would like to ask you something about Mr. Miroslav Tadic. How long have you known Miroslav Tadic, you said something a little bit and how do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've known Miroslav Tadic for almost 30 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, do you know that Mr. Miroslav -- do you know whether Mr. Miroslav Tadic forced you or anybody else to go to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear in Samac about Miroslav Tadic forcing anybody to leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice, in contacts with you, or members of other ethnic groups, behaved differently, did he exhibit any kind of discriminatory behaviour?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about Miroslav Tadic insulting anybody on ethnic grounds or --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, at the end, I would like to ask you, on the 17th of April, 1992 in the morning when you woke up, did you want to leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never thought about leaving Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, did you have an opportunity to leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could have gone on an exchange whenever I wanted, I could have applied to go. At the old pensioner's hall, there was a notice stating that those who wanted to go to Croatian territory and to the other territory, the Bosnian Muslim territory could sign up if they wished to go. I just read that, turned around, and left. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to go in an illegal way through Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I also had that opportunity but I did not want that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a possibility if you went to Croatia to be mobilised into the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well no, I'm not really up for the HVO because I was 61 years old at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, do you live in Bosanski Samac today?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you live in your apartment where you --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I live in my apartment which I bought two years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, this evidence has been repeated. I think you are finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am finished. This was my last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel who wishes to ask the witness questions? I see none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination by the Prosecution. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, you spoke this afternoon about the situation regarding telephones and you said that the telephones were cut off and they were cut off for all citizens?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, how do you know that they were cut off for all citizens?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the building that I lived in. In my building, there are Muslims and people of Serb ethnicity and Croats, nobody had a telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's that, that experience, what happened to you, what you saw in your building, that makes you say that telephones were cut off for all citizens.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also spoke of Crkvina. On the 17th of May, you were taken by police to Crkvina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said first you went to the police station and then you were put on a bus and taken to Crkvina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When we came to Crkvina, we went to the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you were transported, were you, from Bosanski Samac to Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, of what ethnicity were the people who had been taken to Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Croatian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone explain to you why it was that people of Croatian ethnicity had been rounded up and taken to Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody ever explained that to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It must, of course, have been one of the things that was troubling you at the time, you obviously would have wanted to know why it was that people had been rounded up, Croats had been rounded up and taken to Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was clear to me. I know that that was the policy and that's how it ended. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What policy is that, Mr. Borbeli?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: National policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the policy of the new authorities in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Right. Well, you were taken back to Bosanski Samac that very day, I think.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken back to Bosanski Samac, did other Croats remain at Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all returned to Samac in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you returned early in the day?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was returned in the afternoon, perhaps it was about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it that -- well, let me rephrase that. Am I correct that the Croats who had been rounded up and taken to Crkvina had to be taken back in groups, in other words, transport was going to and fro in order to take people back?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were taken to the secondary school gym and again, you said that there were some 300 people there, of what ethnicity --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Only of Croatian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if the people were rounded up and placed in the high school gym on that day, the 17th of May, or was it apparent to you when you got there that the place had already been housing people?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, perhaps there were about ten people there when we went in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And presumably then, people kept coming in, Croats kept coming in until numbers reached around 300; is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. They came every day and then when they all got there, they went for an exchange, those who wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You also said that the people who were there had been arrested for possession of guns. Is it your position that all of these 300 Croats had been rounded up and taken into the high school gym for that reason?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were people from the neighbouring villages who had weapons and when they handed them in, they came there. Perhaps they were about 150 of them but the others, like I was, those without weapons, they were about half as many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did anyone ever tell you why you were in there, why you were being kept there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever told me so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross come along and -- I withdraw that question. Was that part of the policy that you've spoken of?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The rounding up of 300 Croats in the secondary school gym, in your view, was that part of this policy of the new authorities that you've told us about, that you told the Court about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that exactly. I wasn't involved in politics so as far as politics is concerned, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any of the men in the high school gym, yourself included, ever being charged with any criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I just want to ask you about the conditions in the high school gym. How much food were you receiving and the other prisoners, what was your daily allowance?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't enough food. We were given food twice a day, perhaps every other day, there was a cooked meal, but it wasn't enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you lose weight in the three months that you were there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit. I lost a little bit and more because I was upset rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were upset, weren't you, at being rounded up and placed in a prison simply because of the fact that you are a Croat or regarded as being a Croat?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't happy there. I was unhappy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Now, let's just get back to the food. What sort of food were you actually given?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received cooked meals, peas, beans, green beans, goulash, that's as far as cooked food is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that wasn't every day, that was only on every other day, I think you said.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the other prisoners lose weight?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. Perhaps they dropped as much weight as I did. Nobody was that hungry. If they were hungry there was always -- nobody was famished, there was always something to be found to eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the sleeping conditions were -- well in effect there was nothing provided to you for sleeping, no bedding, pillows, blankets or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were mattresses on the floor, but there weren't enough of them. But I sent a message to my relative and she sent me three blankets which I got right away so that there weren't any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The beatings that you described that took place in the -- in the high school gym, who carried out the beatings?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Miljkovic called Lugar came in with a pistol in his hand, in his right hand and later, he found a glass bottle in the hall and he hit people over the head, both with the bottle and the pistol and he kicked them also. And finally, he killed two people and I saw that myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And did this terrify the men who were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Lugar, did other men come in and beat the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on two occasions, but it wasn't really a bad beating, it was just sort of incidental.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the bodies of the men that Lugar killed?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He ordered those who were sleeping next to those people to take the blankets and bring them out into the hall and that is what the people did, took them to the -- out into the hall, that is as much as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that doctors came every other day, is that to treat the prisoners who had been beaten and sustained injuries as a result of beatings?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that didn't happen. People were nervous and -- because they were afraid mostly, they asked for sleeping pills or tranquilizers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see and did the Red Cross distribute sleeping pills and tranquilizers to calm them down?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have sleeping pills and tranquilizers?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is for the re-examination because the witness said that doctors came and the Prosecutor said -- and the witness said the Red Cross so perhaps it would be important to clarify this who brought the medicines, whether it was the doctors, the nurses, or staff of the Red Cross, perhaps this was -- this would be a good thing to clarify. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who handed out the tranquilizers and the sleeping pills, was it the doctors or the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the nurses distributed the medicines to those who asked for them. They were given by doctors, the doctors would prescribe them and then the nurses would distribute them. This is what I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just return briefly to the murders that you described. Can you remember when they took place, the murders committed by Lugar?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to say what date it was exactly but it was in early July 1990 [as interpreted], perhaps -- it was the 5th or the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean July 1992, I think. Can you just tell us, in the transcript Mr. Borbeli, you appear to say that the murders took place in early July 1990, I suggest that you must be mistaken, in fact you must have meant July 1992. I'm correct, aren't I?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And was he alone when he committed these murders or was he in company with other paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was alone. He was in a semi-intoxicated state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And how many guards were there at the high school gym on this occasion when he came in alone?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One guard was outside, the one who was guarding us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard, yes, he had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't want every single detail but how did Lugar actually kill these two men?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were sitting down next to the wall and he fired into the chest the first bullet and the second into the forehead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There must have been blood all over the walls, I assume?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blood started flowing from the top and I saw what was at hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the blood ever cleaned away?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately. Immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm sorry to chop and change, let's just get back to the doctors again. Are you saying, from what you saw, that the doctors were primarily dispensing tranquilizers and sleeping pills?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Approximately when were you taken from the high school gym to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken away in mid-August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the ethnic background of people who were, at that stage, living in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Croatian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Zasavica had always been a Croatian village, had it not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in addition to the people who normally lived there, were there other Croats such as yourself also taken there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see guards at the entrance to the village?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were free to move around if you wanted to take a walk into Bosanski Samac, you could have done so?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could, but I didn't want to move away from there because the job demanded for me to stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you go back to your apartment, go and live there, go and live in Bosanski Samac in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came back from the exchange, then I came back to the apartment and continued to live there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Just one more question before the break, if I may, but I'm not asking about when you came back from the exchange, I'm asking when you were first taken to Zasavica from the high school gym. On that occasion, on that occasion, why didn't you just say well, look, why didn't you just walk back to your apartment in Bosanski Samac if you were free to do so?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't go back to the apartment. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, perhaps I should look at this after the break. It's now 3.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll take our break and continue at 1615 hours. --- Break taken at 3.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, we were talking -- I was asking you before the break about Zasavica. Now, your evidence is that you were taken from the high school gym to Zasavica, you volunteered to go there and you worked there for some 17 days before being taken to the exchange. What I want to know is this: Is there any reason why you didn't leave Zasavica in that 17 days and go back to your apartment, perhaps, to check out and see how it was, what condition it was in, something like that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not go to the apartment. I could not go any further than the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I want to know. In effect, Zasavica was a place where you were allowed to wander about the village but you were restricted in the sense that you couldn't actually leave the --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Could you fix this so that it's louder?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness asked for the volume to be turned up a bit in his headphones because he's a bit hard of hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the usher will help. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just repeat the question that I wanted to ask you because we have to make sure it's clear in this transcript that we're writing here. Tell me if this is correct: You were free to wander about Zasavica but you weren't actually free to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would prevent you from leaving the village?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were you ever told, ever given any reason why you and the other Croats in Zasavica weren't free to leave the town, the little village?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As far as the exchange is concerned, you had never asked to be exchanged; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask, but I did await the exchange. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just give me a moment to confer with my case manager, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to the exchange, the only people that you spoke to about whether or not you would be exchanged were the International Red Cross and Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you'd known Mr. Tadic for some 30 years and he was your friend?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, good acquaintances up to 30 years, for about 30 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And he basically told you that you didn't have to be exchanged if you didn't want to and that you could go back to your home?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's, in fact, what you did, you did go back to your home, you went back to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't go back to --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just wait for me to finish so that you can hear clearly what I've got to -- the question, okay? You, in fact, went back to your home and started living there again, you did not go back to Zasavica or the high school gym?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Tadic was a man of considerable influence, wasn't he, because he could make sure that you didn't have to go back to those places?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, calling for speculation. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you directly. Did Mr. Tadic do anything or say anything that made it clear that you would not be obliged to go back to Zasavica or the high school gym?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked that immediately at the exchange in Dragalic, if I were to return and if I went back to school, or to Zasavica, then I would not go back, then I would proceed further. He said to me, he said the following to me, whoever wants to go to their own homes can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He made that clear to you? Perhaps I will make it clearer for you. Did he make it -- was he speaking to you personally when he said to you that you should go back to your home and not Zasavica or the high school gym?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was addressing us and when I heard that, I decided straight away to go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown D3/3, please. The exchange list that was shown to the witness previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Usher. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now there's some names there of some people, let's have a look at some of them, Dragan Delic, number 20; and Muhamed Bicic number 21; and Dragan Lukac, number 25; and Franjo Barukcic, number 26; did Mr. Tadic tell them that they were free to go back to their homes if they wanted?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this group where I was, by the bus, I mean these people who were there, they knew. But some got out and went immediately towards the exchange, I mean the place of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, all I want to know is this: Did Mr. Tadic make it clear to those men whose names I've just read out, indeed to all of the people who are on this list, that if they wanted to, they could just go back to their homes, back to their homes in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us had that knowledge that whoever wanted to return could, and those who did not want to return, well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that if you'd had to go back to the high school gym or Zasavica, you would have kept on going; in other words, you would have gone through the exchange and into -- crossed over, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's because you - along with all of the other Croats who were in the high school gym, and in Zasavica - didn't like being rounded up and deprived of their freedom, would that be -- is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Number 19 on the list, Janko [phoen] Jurgen. That was a German fellow would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember there being any Germans or foreigner?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes. Yes, there was this German guy with us, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone called for him to be exchanged? On the other side?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware if anyone from the other side, from the Croatian side, had called, had asked for him to be exchanged, just as you were called by your sister and your nephew?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were looking for me in Croatia, I mean my sister, but they could never wait for the exchange for me to be there so the war was over, and I found out about this only in 1996 on the 10th of May when I went to Orasje to meet up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Some of the men whose names are on the list that I showed you, Dragan Lukac, Dragan Delic, Franjo Barukcic, and others, were they showing signs of injury, having been beaten?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Well, Dragan did. I was in the hall with him before entering the bus and he, himself, showed that he had no teeth and I was surprised. Well, the others no, the others didn't have any injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Dragan Delic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the others, any of the men on the bus, show signs of having lost a lot of weight?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, no. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anything new from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: From the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, isn't this a job for the counsel calling the witness to re-examine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's why I was wondering because I thought Mr. Krgovic is still going to re-examine. MR. DI FAZIO: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, are you going to reexamine?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are, all right. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My understanding last time Your Honour, is that if the other counsels would like to have redirect it should be prior to the Defence who called the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If the cross-examination raised something new which was not raised in the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is why I asked you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's my idea to clarify with the witness. Re-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, I am Igor Pantelic, attorney at law --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes I wanted to find out what was new which was raised in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll explain that. The question posed to this witness with regard to Zasavica and about the possible let's say institution or persons who prevented people from Zasavica to go out from -- it was just raised in cross-examination by my learned Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Two questions you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One question, maybe two to clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Borbeli. I'm Igor Pantelic, attorney at law Defence counsel for Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about the possibility of getting out of Zasavica. You said then that the authorities did not allow that. Please be so kind as to tell me whether some passes were needed in order to leave Zasavica. Were you supposed to get a pass if you wanted to leave Zasavica, if you remember, of course?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no need to get out, so I didn't ask for a pass. Actually, people who needed to get something done went to town to Samac, they went, and they came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to them? Did you hear who it was that gave these passes, if they were supposed to have passes?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to the authorities, what is the authorities for you, is it the police, is the police the authorities?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic. Re-examined by Mr. Krgovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, I'm going to put a few questions to you in relation to what you said to the Prosecutor in order to clarify certain matters. If you remember, the Prosecutor asked you how you found out that nobody had their telephones connected, you said that you found out because in your building, all your neighbours irrespective of ethnic background did not have operational telephones and now I'm asking you about your other neighbours who did not live in the same building that you did, members of all ethnic backgrounds, did you hear that their phones went dead at the same time when yours did?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same time, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Well Your Honours please, this is evidence that should have been led in chief. The whole purpose, the whole purpose of Mr. Krgovic's questioning was apparent, we all know why he's asking the questions about the telephones. It's not clarifying anything that I raised regarding the basis of knowledge. I asked him expressly, whether it was based on his experience in that particular building he said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. Don't go outside the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor asked this witness on the basis of what he knew that everybody's telephones went dead in town, irrespective of ethnicity and the witness answered that this was due to the fact that in his building, all the tenants irrespective of ethnicity did not have any telephones working and now I'm asking him whether he had any other information on the basis of which he replied to the Prosecutor. Did he have any other source of information except for the information he had in his very own apartment building. That is what I was after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness already answered this question, I'm going to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Borbeli, when the Prosecutor asked you about the reasons for your detention, you said that it is politics that is to be blamed for that. The Prosecutor asked you whether that was the policies pursued by the newly-established authorities, tell me, did you refer by then to the parties, that took over power in Samac after the multi-party elections, that is to say, the HDZ, the SDA, and the SDS or were you referring to some other authorities, who did you have in mind? MR. DI FAZIO: The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this question either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean you do not understand this question?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this question is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you which politics you had in mind, you said that politics led to your detention, remember that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the Prosecutor asked you which politics you had in mind, which policies, the policies of the newly established authorities?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The newly established authorities of the SDS, there was no other authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about detention in Crkvina and you said that many people were there from Crkvina, I mean that there were many people at the stadium in Crkvina. These people who came from Crkvina to Samac together with you, were they the same people who had previously left or were there people who were not brought to Samac at all but rather were brought directly from the villages to Samac to the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for those who were with me in Crkvina, they were brought with me and later on, people came from villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that some people who were in Crkvina, women and children, were released later, did you see them in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only women were released as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they released, were they allowed to go home?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them in Samac later?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was still in detention. They were not in detention for a long time, they were there for a very short while and then they were released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another thing I wanted to ask you, the Prosecutor asked you about food. Tell me, until the Red Cross started giving you food, did you personally get food from home, did any of your friends or relatives bring you food?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BORBELI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My relative brought me food and that was almost enough for me while I was at the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Borbeli. We are finished with the evidence required from you so you can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we call in a new witness, if I may address the Chamber regarding protective measures but before that, could we move to a private session in order for me to explain the reasons why I am requesting such measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, let's move to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
